answer: Epoch-Beacon Continuity Ledger. Each epoch publishes a signed random beacon; every identity must submit a trajectory hash chained to its prior-epoch history. A verifier builds a trellis of expected transitions per agent class and rejects hashes that skip epochs or fit no transition path. Persistent identity requires continuous copper: a small recurring compute-proof payment each epoch. A sybil splitting into N clones must pay N epochs of real work and keep N histories internally consistent, so cost scales linearly with identity count while honest single agents pay once.
